A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DPO and the same three evaluation tasks. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5, Figure 1 and Table 1 report original evaluation results for DPO and six baselines on three tasks.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original benchmark results, including comparisons against twelve baselines and ten-seed results in Table 4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces Gθ=A·dgθ with Gθ=Id+ΔS∇gθ and adds the time step Δ as an input. This revises the specified operator construction, while stagewise sampling, replay targets and smooth L1 training remain unchanged. v2 Corollary 3 already discussed Euler-form dynamics, making this a limited correction of the written procedure.

E1.justification: Materials deformation and topological materials deformation are renamed surface modeling and grid-based modeling. The evaluated boundary-spline, grid-function and octa-alanine dihedral tasks remain. Broader application examples in v3 Section 2.3 are not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: v3 adds DDPG, CrossQ and TQC, each with standard and reshaped rewards, expanding the evaluated baseline set from six to twelve. TRPO, PPO and SAC retain both reward variants; v2's Straight prefix becomes S-.

E3.justification: Table 2 retains the episode counts, steps per episode and reward factors. However, v3 states 5,000 molecular training steps while retaining 800×6=4,800 in the table. Its newly listed step sizes also conflict with the stated relation T=HΔ=1. The PDFs do not resolve whether settings changed or these are documentation inconsistencies.

E4.justification: v3 adds computational-efficiency analysis, including the model-size comparison in Appendix C.2 and Table 3. It also extends the existing standard-versus-reshaped reward comparison to DDPG, CrossQ and TQC, adding supplementary evidence within the retained tasks.

E5.justification: v2 reports 200 test episodes and trajectory uncertainty without specifying repeated training seeds or significance tests. v3 Appendix C.3 first reports ten random seeds, mean±standard-deviation results in Table 4 and t-tests on seed-level means. This establishes new statistical reporting, not an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds six baseline variants and changes retained baseline values: surface PPO changes from 19.229 to 20.61, and Straight/S-PPO from 15.117 to 19.17. DPO's 6.323, 6.061 and 53.340 are merely rounded in v3. Table 4 adds ten-seed results, and Appendix C.3 reports comparable surface performance between DPO and CrossQ. These additions do not establish a same-setting DPO performance gain.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the specialized time-weighted Lagrangian derivation and Nesterov-flow remark with a general continuous-control Hamiltonian, stationarity conditions and explicit Euler discretization in Sections 2.1–2.3. It revises the specialized score expression and adds an O(H²ε^-6) computational-cost derivation. The main convergence, sample-complexity and regret bounds and their proofs are largely retained, with substantial material moved to Appendix B.

C1.justification: The central Differential RL, DPO and pointwise-convergence contributions remain. v3 makes physics consistency without explicit constraints an explicit headline claim and presents O(K^5/6) without qualification in the abstract and conclusion. That rate already appeared in v2, and its restricted-hypothesis conditions remain in v3's theory.

C2.justification: v3 adds tentative explanations involving PPO instability and SAC entropy regularization, and acknowledges that DPO trajectories are not always smooth. Appendix D newly states that discontinuous dynamics are excluded and qualifies generality beyond the three tested domains. These refine the interpretation and limitations of retained findings.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly discloses numerical step sizes and per-method model sizes. Section 4.2 adds instructions for accessing trained artifacts through the repository README. The code URL, A100 hardware, episode counts and reward factors carry over from v2; no architectural change is established by the new size disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 removes v2's extended positioning against Lipschitz-MDP, smooth-MDP and kernelized regret bounds, including the cited comparisons with Maran et al. and Vakili and Olkhovskaya. It adds DDPG, CrossQ and TQC references and substantially refocuses positioning on scientific computing and physics priors. The model-based RL access and replanning critique is retained but moved into the introduction.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Standard RL now precedes the differential formulation, supporting lemmas and the full convergence proof move into Appendix B, and computational-details and limitations appendices are added. The declarations are also substantially condensed.

P2.justification: The document is retypeset with different typography, margins and table formatting. Figure 1 is redrawn for thirteen algorithms. Table 1 is transposed and groups standard and reshaped methods; Table 2 moves to Appendix C with an additional row, and Tables 3–4 add model-size and statistical displays.

improvement.justification: Broader baselines, ten-seed statistics and explicit limitations strengthen empirical reporting. However, v3 Section 2.3 defines hf=0.5||p||²-r; substituting its stated reward cancels the kinetic term, conflicting with its own Hamiltonian definition and replacing v2's kinetic-plus-potential expression. Together with inconsistent training-setting disclosures, this creates uncertainty about the revised method's reliability. The PDFs do not establish whether these errors affect implementation, so the benefits and harms do not support a confident net quality judgment.
